sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 34.8% a year from $404.5 million in FY2016 to $5.93 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196].

The shape is a decelerating ramp: growth ran 104.0% in FY2017 and 64.2% in FY2021, then fell to 11.8% in FY2022 and 0.1% in FY2023 before recovering to 16.4% in FY2024 and 10.6% in FY2025 [D36][D218][D263][D311][D358][D406].
The FY2017 loss of $3.45 billion was driven by a $2.6 billion increase in stock-based compensation tied to the CEO award and IPO-related RSUs [F32][P74].
The operating loss narrowed from $1.40 billion in FY2023 to $532 million in FY2025, lifting operating margin from -30.4% to -9.0% [F18][F20][F28][F30].
In FY2025 advertising revenue of $5.19 billion contributed 5.3pp of revenue growth, while other revenue of $745 million contributed 5.4pp [S39][S42][D538][D545].

The advertising increase came from roughly 17% more impressions, largely in Sponsored Snaps and Spotlight, partly offset by a roughly 10% lower cost per impression; other revenue rose on subscription growth [P24].
Other revenue's share of revenue rose from 4.3% in FY2023 to 12.6% in FY2025, so the largest single driver is no longer advertising alone [D539][D543].
Operating costs grew 5.5pp slower than revenue in FY2025, at 5.1%, and incremental operating margin was 44.8% [D430][D423][D429].
The diluted share count rose 2.1% in FY2025, so the 35.7% smaller loss per share outpaced the 34.0% smaller net loss [D425][D409][D408].
Operating margin of -9.0% in FY2025 is the window high, above the -32.4% median and far above the -422.5% low of FY2017 [F30][D554][D555][D553].
The FY2025 bridge was led by cost of revenue adding 1.1pp, R&D 1.3pp and other lines 3.3pp [D431][D432][D433].

Sales and marketing fell $42.4 million on prior-year marketing timing, lower advertising spend and $19.9 million of FY2024 restructuring, while R&D rose $101.9 million on product development headcount [P22][P23].
In FY2025 net margin of -7.8% sat 1.2pp above the -9.0% operating margin, helped by $68.9 million of other income that included $96.7 million of debt extinguishment gains [F50][F30][D591][X130][P18].

Operating cash flow of $656 million in FY2025 exceeded the $460 million net loss, and free cash flow of $437 million was a 7.4% margin, the window high against a -4.1% median [F80][F40][F100][D393][D560][D561].
Operating cash flow rose on non-cash items, including $1.0 billion of stock-based compensation and $163.6 million of depreciation and amortization, plus working-capital timing [P13].
Capex of $219 million was 3.7% of revenue and 1.34x D&A, and the filing attributes it mainly to leased-facility improvements [F90][D392][D395][P10].
Stock-based compensation was 155.0% of operating cash flow in FY2025, down from 251.8% in FY2024 [D396][D348].
The company moved to net debt of $596 million in FY2025, net cash of -10.1% of revenue against a 45.0% peer median, the 0th percentile of five internet peers [D399][D400][D579][D578].
In February 2025 it issued $1.50 billion of 2033 Notes and repurchased $1.4 billion of 2026, 2027 and 2028 Notes, leaving total debt at $3.54 billion [P2][P1][D398].
Buybacks of $751 million were 171.7% of free cash flow in FY2025, and the diluted share count still rose 2.1% [D401][D402][D425].
Liquidity is $2.94 billion of cash and investments against a current ratio of 3.56x, the window low [D397][F180][D565].
The company has posted a net loss in each of the last ten years, from $515 million in FY2016 to $460 million in FY2025 [R1][F31][F40].
The loss is narrowing, but ten straight loss years mean profitability still rests on non-GAAP adjustments rather than reported earnings [R1].
Stock-based compensation was 17.1% of revenue in FY2025 and at least 10% in each of the last nine years [R2][D390][D22][D66][D110][D155][D202][D247][D295][D342].
At 191.1% of the operating loss, stock-based compensation is the main reason the GAAP loss persists while cash flow turns positive [R2][D404].
Net cash fell for a fourth straight year into net debt of $596 million in FY2025, from net cash of $1.44 billion in FY2021 [R3][D399][D211].
Buybacks of 171.7% of free cash flow while net cash turns negative is the capital-allocation tension to watch [R4][D402].
Whether operating margin in the FY2026 10-K holds above the -9.0% FY2025 level or slips back toward the -32.4% median [F30][D555].
Whether net cash as a share of revenue in the FY2026 10-K improves from -10.1% or extends the four-year decline [D400][R3].
Whether stock-based compensation as a share of revenue in the FY2026 10-K falls below the 17.1% FY2025 level [D390].
